headline: Sartorius writedown drives a steep net loss on steady sales
summary_short: Bio-Rad's Q1 2026 revenue was roughly flat at $592.1M (+1.1% y/y, -14.6% q/q), but a $727.7M unrealized fair-value loss on its Sartorius AG equity stake drove net income to a $527.1M loss from a $64M profit a year ago.
summary_long: Revenue was roughly flat at $592.1M (+1.1% y/y), with underlying (currency-neutral) sales down in both segments — Life Science essentially flat on soft academic research demand, Clinical Diagnostics up 1.9% on FX but down organically on Middle East conflict disruption in EMEA. Gross margin held at 52.3%; operating income rose 43.9% y/y to $34.1M as R&D fell on lower restructuring costs. The quarter's headline is non-operating: a $727.7M unrealized fair-value loss on Bio-Rad's Sartorius AG stake (accounting-only, no cash impact) drove EBIT to -$677.5M and net income to a $527.1M loss versus a $64M profit a year ago. Bio-Rad repurchased $47.8M of stock and held $1.56B in cash plus short-term investments at quarter-end. No numeric FY2026 guidance was given.

drivers.explanation: A $727.7M non-cash fair-value loss on the Sartorius AG equity stake overwhelmed an otherwise stable operating quarter, driving EBIT and net income sharply negative.
Currency-neutral sales fell in both segments — Life Science on soft academic research demand, Clinical Diagnostics on Middle East conflict disruption in EMEA — offsetting FX benefit.

Consolidated gross margin held at 52.3%; Life Science margin fell ~0.3ppt on higher material and fuel-related logistics costs, offset by Clinical Diagnostics' ~0.2ppt gain from lower scrap and restructuring costs.
R&D expense fell to 10.6% of sales from 12.6% on lower restructuring costs, lifting operating income y/y even as SG&A rose modestly on FX impact on the international cost base.
The swing to a large EBIT loss is driven almost entirely by the $727.7M unrealized Sartorius AG fair-value loss, which flows through pre-tax income even as core operations improved.
